history.dynasty: Modern — revived in 1951 by Mahavir Dal devotees; no royal dynasty
history.period: Ancient shrine tradition (legend); present structure built after 1951
history.summary: TOWN CORRECTION: CSV lists the town as Bathinda, but the temple stands at Maiser Khana village, about 29 km from Bathinda on the Bathinda–Mansa Road (also described as towards Talwandi Sabo and near Maur Mandi; PIN 151509). District Bathinda is correct; the village is served by the Maiser Khana post office under Talwandi Sabo. Maiser Khana is a temple honouring the goddesses Durga and Jwala Ji. Legend holds that a devotee named Kamala, unable to undertake the hazardous pilgrimage to far-off Jwala Ji, performed lifelong penance to honour Durga for her darshan; the goddess was pleased and granted him a vision twice a year — hence the two grand melas held each year on Ashtami. Devotees gather from across Punjab and nearby states to sing hymns in praise of the deity; the gathering is noted as politically significant because Sikhs and Hindus attend with equal enthusiasm. The old shrine had decayed by 1951 through government indifference, when devotees asked the Mahavir Dal to take it over; Radheshyam Budhlada, Jagannath ji of Maur Mandi and Hansraj Aggarwal collected funds and hired India's best architects to build the present temple. The Bathinda administration listed it as one of nine spots to be developed to make the district a religious-tourism hub.

name: Maiser Khana Temple
town_description: Maiser Khana is a village on the Bathinda–Mansa Road in Bathinda district, about 29 km from Bathinda city, known almost entirely for this Durga–Jwala Ji shrine and its twice-yearly Ashtami melas.

travel.airport: Bathinda Airport has limited service (verify); the nearest major airport is Chandigarh (~230 km, verify).
travel.railway: Bathinda Junction (~29 km); taxis and buses run towards Maur Mandi / Talwandi Sabo / Mansa.
travel.road: On the Bathinda–Mansa Road, 29 km from Bathinda, reached via Maur Mandi / Talwandi Sabo; the last approach is through narrow village lanes (verify signage).

visitor_information.best_time: October to March for pleasant weather; the two Ashtami melas for the full experience (very crowded).
